description_good_justification: README.md opening line succinctly states purpose: 'C2PA manifest embedding, hard binding, and validation for structured text formats using ASCII armour delimiters.' Same text is the crates.io description in Cargo.toml.
interact_justification: README.md 'Quick Start' explains obtaining the crate (cargo/npm/pip); CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Issues' and 'Submitting Changes' explain feedback/contribution; .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml give structured feedback channels; GitHub surfaces CONTRIBUTING.md automatically in the issue/PR creation flow.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' section: fork, branch from main, add tests, run cargo test/clippy/fmt, open a PR. PRs are the stated process; .github/pull_request_template.md exists.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies acceptance requirements: cargo test --all-features must pass, cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings must be clean, cargo fmt --all -- --check must pass, and Conventional Commits style is required for commit messages.
floss_license_justification: Cargo.toml: license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; both are OSI-approved FLOSS licenses.
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT and Apache-2.0 are both on the OSI-approved license list (https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT, https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0).
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT hold the full texts (dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per Cargo.toml); a top-level LICENSE file (identical to LICENSE-APACHE) is also present at the repository root for tooling that only recognizes that exact filename.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md covers Overview, Quick Start, embed/extract examples, hard binding, feature flags, supported formats, and links to docs.rs; crate also carries #![warn(missing_docs)] (src/lib.rs:96) enforcing rustdoc coverage.
documentation_interface_justification: Public API (embed_manifest, extract_manifest, classify_reference, hardbinding::compute_data_hash/verify_data_hash, bridge::validate) is documented via rustdoc published at docs.rs/c2pa-structured-text (linked from README badge), plus worked examples in README.md.
sites_https_justification: Repo URL https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text, crates.io, docs.rs, npm, and PyPI are all HTTPS-only services; no plain-HTTP project site is used.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled (gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text --jq .hasIssuesEnabled = true) and is public, URL-addressable, searchable, and open to any GitHub account with no proprietary client required. GitHub Discussions is not enabled (hasDiscussionsEnabled: false), but Issues alone satisfies this criterion.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, issue templates, code comments) is in English.
maintained_justification: git log shows active commits through 2026-08-22 (most recent: 747e83e); two tagged releases in 2026 (v0.2.0 on 2026-08-02, v0.3.0 on 2026-07-13 per git log --format=%cd); Dependabot PRs merged/handled weekly through 2026-08-24 per gh api issues listing.
repo_public_justification: gh repo view writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text --json isPrivate reports isPrivate: false; repo is at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text.
repo_track_justification: Git repository; git log shows author, committer, timestamp, and commit hash for every change (e.g. '747e83e docs: add title and tagline...' by David Condrey <davidcondrey@me.com>).
repo_interim_justification: git log --oneline shows dozens of commits between the v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 tags (e.g. a6f48b5, 620c681, a76b946), not just tag-point commits.
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed VCS; repo hosted on GitHub with full clone history available (git clone https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text.git).
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml version = "0.3.0"; each release has a distinct version enforced by release.yml's 'Tag matches Cargo.toml version' check, which fails the release job if the pushed tag doesn't match Cargo.toml's version field.
version_semver_justification: Versions follow SemVer (0.2.0, 0.3.0) as declared in Cargo.toml and enforced by release.yml's tag/version match check.
version_tags_justification: git tag shows v0.2.0 and v0.3.0; release.yml triggers on push of tags matching 'v*'.
release_notes_justification: GitHub releases for v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 (gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text/releases) are produced by release.yml's softprops/action-gh-release step with generate_release_notes: true, which is GitHub's auto-generated 'What's Changed' list of merged PRs/commits, not human-authored, curated release notes. No CHANGELOG.md is committed to the repo (git log --all -- CHANGELOG.md returns nothing) despite a changelog.yml workflow existing to generate one on push to main.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in any release to date, so there is nothing for release notes to identify.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled with structured templates: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml; CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Issues' documents the process.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used as the tracker; issues #1 and #2 (gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text/issues?state=all) are individually tracked, labeled, and closed there.
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: Only two issues have ever been filed (#1 'Add doc-tests for supported structured text formats', #2 'Define which structured text formats are supported'), both maintainer-filed (dcondrey) on 2026-06-24 and both closed 2026-07-13. No externally-filed bug reports exist in the 2-12 month window, so there is no backlog of unacknowledged reports (vacuously satisfied: majority of zero reports is trivially acknowledged).). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: Same evidence as report_responses: the only enhancement-shaped issue on record (#2, defining supported formats) was addressed and closed by the maintainer; no outstanding unanswered enhancement requests exist (vacuously satisfied).). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues history (open and closed) is public and searchable at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text/issues?q=is%3Aissue, with no login required to view.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process: private GitHub Security Advisory (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text/security/advisories/new) or email admin@writerslogic.com; linked from README.md 'Security' section and CONTRIBUTING.md.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md explicitly names two private channels: GitHub Security Advisories (private by design) and direct email to admin@writerslogic.com, with guidance to avoid public issues.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months (no security advisories or CVEs on record for this repo), so there is no response-time data to evaluate.
build_justification: Rust crate requires a build step (cargo build); .github/workflows/ci.yml automates it via 'cargo clippy'/'cargo test' jobs, and release.yml automates the publish build (cargo publish, wasm-pack build, maturin build) triggered by version tags.
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, plus wasm-pack and maturin, the standard tools for wasm-bindgen and PyO3 bindings respectively — all conventional for this ecosystem.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, wasm-pack, and maturin are all FLOSS (MIT/Apache-2.0). No proprietary toolchain is required, as confirmed by ci.yml using only dtolnay/rust-toolchain, jetli/wasm-pack-action, and PyO3/maturin-action.
test_justification: Automated FLOSS test suite via 'cargo test' (Rust's built-in test framework, MIT/Apache-2.0). tests/e2e.rs and tests/matrix.rs plus inline #[test] functions in src/embed.rs, src/extract.rs, src/codec.rs, src/error.rs, src/hardbinding.rs. CONTRIBUTING.md documents how to run it: 'cargo test' / 'cargo test --all-features'.
test_invocation_justification: 'cargo test' is the standard, idiomatic test invocation for Rust; documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and run in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml 'test' job: cargo test --features "$NATIVE_FEATURES").
test_most_justification: 41 #[test] functions exist across src/ and tests/ (embed.rs:7, extract.rs:8, codec.rs:4, error.rs:4, hardbinding.rs:9, tests/e2e.rs:4, tests/matrix.rs:5), but no coverage measurement tool (e.g. cargo-tarpaulin, cargo-llvm-cov, codecov) is configured in CI, so branch/input coverage cannot be substantiated with evidence.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the 'test' job (cargo test) on every push to main and every pull request; recent runs confirmed green via gh run list --workflow=ci.yml (all 'completed success').
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2: 'Make changes, add tests, run cargo test --all-features' is an explicit stated policy that changes include tests.
tests_are_added_justification: Commit a76b946 'feat: uniform Error::code, verified MSRV, and integration tests' and the addition of tests/e2e.rs and tests/matrix.rs alongside feature commits show the test-with-change policy was followed in recent major changes.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explicitly documents the add-tests requirement as step 2 of 'Submitting Changes', directly in the contribution instructions.
warnings_justification: Clippy (FLOSS Rust linter) is enabled and run in CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml 'check' job runs 'cargo clippy --all-targets --features "$NATIVE_FEATURES" -- -D warnings' plus separate clippy runs for the wasm and python feature sets; cargo fmt --all -- --check also enforced.
warnings_fixed_justification: clippy is run with '-D warnings' (deny, not just warn) in ci.yml and release.yml, meaning any clippy warning fails the build; recent CI runs are green (gh run list --workflow=ci.yml shows 'completed success'), so no outstanding warnings exist on main.
warnings_strict_justification: src/lib.rs:95 '#![forbid(unsafe_code)]' and src/lib.rs:96 '#![warn(missing_docs)]' are crate-wide strict lints beyond default clippy, combined with '-D warnings' in CI across all three feature-set builds (native, wasm, python).
know_secure_design_justification: README.md 'Fragility — and the soft-binding recovery path' section shows deliberate security-relevant design reasoning (byte-exact hash binding, explicit non-goals, pairing with soft binding for durability); the crate explicitly delegates cryptographic signature/trust validation to c2pa-rs rather than reimplementing it ('this crate does *not* reimplement' — README.md line 27); src/lib.rs:95 forbids unsafe code crate-wide.
know_common_errors_justification: Design decisions demonstrate awareness of common structured-text/text-processing vulnerability classes: explicit rejection of bare-CR line endings, deliberate no-Unicode-normalization to avoid false-match/false-mismatch bugs (README.md 'The Hard Binding' section), and security-labeled fix commits (f138038 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29', eda92ba 'fix(security): autofix 3rd party Github Actions should be pinned', 7ca84bd 'ci(security): pin actions by SHA and drop GITHUB_TOKEN to read').
crypto_published_justification: src/hardbinding.rs uses only SHA-256/384/512 (Algorithm enum, lines 157-191) via the 'sha2' crate — all publicly published, widely reviewed NIST-standard hash algorithms. Signature/trust cryptography is delegated entirely to c2pa-rs, itself built on published, reviewed algorithms.
crypto_call_justification: src/hardbinding.rs calls the dedicated 'sha2' crate (Sha256::digest, Sha384::digest, Sha512::digest) rather than reimplementing hash algorithms; signature/trust validation is delegated to the c2pa-rs crate rather than reimplemented (README.md: 'a validation bridge to c2pa-rs... which this crate does not reimplement').
crypto_floss_justification: 'sha2' (dual MIT/Apache-2.0) and 'c2pa' (Apache-2.0) are both FLOSS crates, as declared in Cargo.toml [dependencies].
crypto_keylength_justification: This crate performs no key generation or key exchange itself; it only computes/verifies content hashes (SHA-256/384/512) and delegates all signature/trust-chain key handling to c2pa-rs.
crypto_working_justification: src/hardbinding.rs Algorithm enum (lines 157-191) offers only Sha256/Sha384/Sha512; no MD4, MD5, single-DES, RC4, or Dual_EC_DRBG appears anywhere in src/ (grep confirms no such references).
crypto_weaknesses_justification: Only SHA-256/384/512 are used by default (src/hardbinding.rs); no SHA-1 or CBC-mode cipher usage exists in the crate's own code (grep of src/ for sha1/SHA1 finds no matches).
crypto_pfs_justification: This crate performs no key agreement/exchange; it is a content-hashing and manifest-embedding library, not a transport/session-security protocol implementation.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The crate stores no passwords; it has no authentication or credential-storage functionality of any kind.
crypto_random_justification: The crate generates no cryptographic keys or nonces itself; hashing is deterministic (SHA-2 over supplied bytes), and any key/nonce generation for signing is delegated to c2pa-rs.
delivery_mitm_justification: Package delivery is via crates.io, npm, and PyPI, all served exclusively over HTTPS; release.yml publishes via 'cargo publish', 'npm publish', and PyO3/maturin-action's PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC over HTTPS), none of which use plain HTTP.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash-only integrity check delivered over plain HTTP is used anywhere; all package registries (crates.io, npm, PyPI) and the GitHub repo are HTTPS-only, and PyPI publishing uses OIDC Trusted Publishing rather than a bare hash check.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No open, unpatched medium-or-higher severity vulnerability has been publicly reported against this repo (no GitHub security advisories on record); GitHub secret scanning, Dependabot version updates, and OpenSSF Scorecard are active per .github/dependabot.yml and .github/workflows/scorecard.yml.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Security-labeled fixes were shipped promptly when identified, e.g. commit f138038 'fix(security): bump pyo3 to 0.29' and eda92ba 'fix(security): autofix 3rd party Github Actions should be pinned' (#16); no critical vulnerability has gone unaddressed.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Manual grep of the repo for private-key headers (BEGIN RSA/EC/OPENSSH/PRIVATE KEY), AWS key patterns, and Slack tokens found no matches outside the test fixture tests/fixtures/certs/ (which contains only a public test certificate, es256.pub, and its associated non-secret test key material for signature-verification tests, not a production credential). GitHub's secret_scanning is enabled with push_protection enabled (gh api repos/writerslogic/c2pa-structured-text --jq .security_and_analysis: secret_scanning status 'enabled', secret_scanning_push_protection status 'enabled').
static_analysis_justification: Clippy, the standard FLOSS static analyzer for Rust, is run on every push/PR and before every tagged release: .github/workflows/ci.yml 'check' job and release.yml 'verify' job both run 'cargo clippy --all-targets --features "$NATIVE_FEATURES" -- -D warnings' plus wasm/python feature variants.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Only default/standard clippy lints are run (-D warnings on the base lint set); no vulnerability-focused static analysis tool (e.g. CodeQL, cargo-audit, cargo-deny) is configured. A commit message (017a6eb) mentions adding CodeQL, but no CodeQL workflow file exists in .github/workflows/ today (grep for 'codeql' only matches scorecard.yml's unrelated codeql-action/upload-sarif step, which uploads Scorecard's own SARIF output, not a CodeQL code-scan).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: clippy runs with '-D warnings' in both ci.yml and release.yml, so any medium+ finding blocks merge/release by construction; current CI runs are green (gh run list --workflow=ci.yml shows recent 'completed success' runs).
static_analysis_often_justification: Clippy runs on push to main and on pull requests (ci.yml triggers: push branches [main], pull_request branches [main]), but there is no scheduled/daily run independent of commits, so it is not running 'at least daily' when there is no commit activity.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (e.g. sanitizers, fuzzing) is configured anywhere in .github/workflows/ or Cargo.toml; only clippy (static) and cargo test (functional, not dynamic-analysis-instrumented) are run.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: src/lib.rs:95 declares '#![forbid(unsafe_code)]', so the crate contains no memory-unsafe (unsafe) Rust code to require memory-safety dynamic analysis.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis configuration exists at all (see dynamic_analysis above), so no assertion-enabling configuration for such a tool exists either.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is run against this project, so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to fix.
